title: Dendera Temple complex
visualBrief: Dendera medium-fi complex: stepped Hathor temple with six front Hathor-headed columns and twenty-four-column hypostyle hall, roof kiosk/chapel rooms and stairs, roofed Roman mammisi, roofless older mammisi, Coptic basilica and sanatorium ruins, surviving Isis chamber/forecourt, dry sacred-lake basin, north stone portal and eroded mudbrick precinct. Exterior visualization from ordinary pictures and standard PMTiles; inner chambers, crypts, exact reliefs and surveyed archaeological levels are outside scope.

sourceFacts.horizontalBasis: Q735254/way216932198 identifies the entire archaeological complex. PMTiles building35184538738193 provides the8-vertex Hathor temple footprint, and35185840606911 its front hall. The front opening follows the north-northeast end of the mapped outline and the ordinary frontal photograph. The large archaeological-site boundary is context, not a mudbrick wall line.
sourceFacts.architecturalHeights: Photographic proportions estimate the43.6m-wide front at approximately18.4m including its cavetto cornice, with a lower13.75m rear roof. The retained PMTiles tags8m for the main building and5m for its front part contradict the observed facade proportions; they remain recorded, not silently treated as measured architecture. Column heights, capitals, bays and tiers are draft estimates; no survey or archival source was pursued.

reconstruction.terrainBasis: Reviewed approximate exterior fit on the unchanged standard161-square/6m Mapzen grid. SourceY0 is the original raw-map anchor sample; the primary floor follows its front approach at sourceY7.1. Bounded openings beneath the primary stepped footprint and dry lake are covered by opaque geometry at all four levels. Other monument floors sit above their sampled local maximum, with retaining foundations. Seven mapped temple/roof/sanatorium records are selectively replaced; seven independent facilities/structures are preserved byte-for-byte in the retained site fixture. Numerical boundary remnants are below1e-7m². Failed loading restores all14 native records and original ground; eviction frees geometry. No native water is present or removed. No exact archaeological thresholds, excavated strata or terrain survey are claimed.
reconstruction.roofBasis: Four original layer1 PMTiles parts constrain the southwest Hathor kiosk and roof chapel/stair-room masses. The2015 roof overview shows the lower terrace, chapel remains, side stair exits and diagonal upper stair; the2020 kiosk photo shows six Hathor columns, screen walls, raised doorway and heavy lintels. Heights, passage dimensions, present crest damage and decorative surfaces are proportional reconstructions, not surveys. The photographed damaged capitals guide defaced masks; invented intact eyes/noses are removed. Fine glyphs and exact erasure patterns are not reproduced.

reconstruction.componentBasis: Ancillary POIs constrain the Roman and older mammisi, basilica and sanatorium. The unmeasured ordinary visitor diagram provides relative axes and approximate dimensions; ordinary photographs show a roofed Roman mammisi, roofless older mammisi/basilica/sanatorium, partially roofed Isis chamber and dry sacred lake. Isis, lake, north portal and mudbrick wall positions remain visual estimates. The archaeological tourism boundary is not used as an ancient wall survey. The precinct is an eroded tapering mudbrick circuit with a north gate opening, not a clean extrusion of the managed-site boundary. Individual damage patterns, carved portraits and hieroglyphs are not reproduced.
